acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each patch function performs compare-and-swap on text content and/or attributes — it does not replace the parent element or trigger a full subtree rebuild
_patchProjectStatus uses statusBadge() / UI.badge() to render badge HTML, consistent with the initial render path
_patchWpRow locates WP rows by data attribute or index and updates only the status badge and pipeline track cells, leaving the WP ID and assigned-to cells untouched
_patchSynthesisLink(true) makes the synthesis link visible (injecting it if not present); _patchSynthesisLink(false) hides it
All patch functions perform fresh DOM queries on each invocation — no cached element references are stored across poll cycles
All new HTML rendered in patch functions uses UI.badge(), UI.card(), UI.banner(), or statusBadge() where applicable (zero raw <span class="badge ..."> strings unless those helpers are insufficient)

summary: Added `data-wp-id` attribute to all WP `<tr>` rows in `renderProjectDetail` for stable row lookup.
Added `.wp-status-cell` and `.wp-pipeline-track-cell` CSS classes to respective `<td>` cells for targeted cell patching.
Wrapped the status badge in `<span id='project-status-badge'>` in the page header for in-place patching.
Wrapped timing info (duration, active time, pipeline runs) in `<span id='timing-info'>` with inner spans `timing-duration`, `timing-active`, `timing-runs` for granular text patching.
Pre-rendered synthesis link row unconditionally with `id='synthesis-link-row'`: visible when `synthesis_generated=true`, hidden (`display:none`) otherwise.
Implemented `_patchProjectStatus(newStatus)` — fresh getElementById each call, compare-and-swap on innerHTML using `statusBadge()`.

Implemented `_patchWpRow(wpId, newStatus, newPipelineTrack)` — locates row via `tr[data-wp-id]` attribute selector; patches `.wp-status-cell` and `.wp-pipeline-track-cell` independently using compare-and-swap.
Implemented `_patchSynthesisLink(visible, repo, slug)` — shows/hides the pre-rendered row; injects a new row if somehow absent when `visible=true`.
Implemented `_patchHealthBadge(health)` — updates `#health-badge` textContent and className; mirrors the logic in the initial render.
Implemented `_patchTimingInfo(timing)` — patches `#timing-duration`, `#timing-active`, `#timing-runs` individually with compare-and-swap on textContent.
Replaced `CSS.escape` with `escapeHtml` for the attribute-selector query in `_patchWpRow` to avoid a modern-browser-only dependency.
Syntax verified: `node --check` passes with exit code 0.

comments.note: `buildRunBadges` in project-detail.js (line ~102) uses raw `<span class="badge badge-in-progress">` and `<span class="badge badge-dry-run">` strings rather than `UI.badge()`. This is a pre-existing inconsistency with the helper convention — not introduced by this WP. Consider migrating to `UI.badge('in-progress', 'Running')` and `UI.badge('dry-run', 'Dry Run')` in a future pass.

`_patchHealthBadge` duplicates the health-badge render logic that already exists inline in `renderProjectDetail` (~line 756 in original). A future consolidation could have the initial render call `_patchHealthBadge` after setting the element's initial state, eliminating the duplication.

The synthesis link injection fallback in `_patchSynthesisLink` uses `document.querySelector('.card-title')` which targets the first `.card-title` on the page. Since the synthesis row is now always pre-rendered (visible or hidden), this path should never fire in practice — but if it did, the insertion point is fragile. Consider adding a more specific landmark ID to the page if this path is ever needed.

comments.note: _patchHealthBadge (lines 351–366) duplicates the identical health-badge rendering logic in the inline callback at lines 758–771 inside renderProjectDetail. The two blocks use the same textContent strings, same CSS class names, and same plural-form logic. This duplication is intentional for now per the Developer's own note, but it is a maintenance surface: a future rename of 'health-badge healthy' or 'health-badge attention' would require two separate edits. A follow-up refactor could have the initial render delegate to _patchHealthBadge after element creation, eliminating the duplicate branch.

_patchSynthesisLink injection fallback (lines 330–338): when visible=true and the synthesis-link-row element is absent, the function inserts the new row before the first document.querySelector('.card-title') — the first card-title on the entire page, not necessarily the 'Work Packages' heading. Since the synthesis-link-row is always pre-rendered unconditionally (visible or hidden) by renderProjectDetail, this path is dead code in practice. Low risk, but if the pre-render contract ever changes this insertion point would be silently fragile.
